PRENATAL GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT: [redacted name]
DATE OF BIRTH: [redacted date]
SAMPLE TYPE: Chorionic villus sample (CVS)
DATE COLLECTED: [redacted date]
DATE REPORTED: [redacted date]
REFERRING PHYSICIAN: Dr. [redacted name]

REFERRAL REASON
Prenatal diagnosis requested for current pregnancy due to previous pregnancy affected with TUBA1A-related Lissencephaly. The previous pregnancy was found to carry a heterozygous TUBA1A c.197T>C p.(Val66Ala) likely pathogenic variant.

METHODOLOGY
1. Sanger Sequencing: Targeted sequencing of TUBA1A exon 2 was performed to detect the familial c.197T>C p.(Val66Ala) variant. DNA was extracted from cultured chorionic villi cells. PCR amplification followed by bidirectional Sanger sequencing was performed using standard protocols.

2. Maternal Cell Contamination (MCC) Analysis: PCR-based analysis of polymorphic markers was performed to exclude maternal cell contamination in the fetal sample. The assay has a detection threshold of approximately 10% maternal contamination.

RESULTS
TUBA1A Gene Analysis (NM_006009.3):
- The familial TUBA1A c.197T>C p.(Val66Ala) variant was NOT DETECTED in the fetal sample
- Sequencing quality was adequate across the region of interest
- Coverage: 100% of coding region analyzed

Maternal Cell Contamination Analysis:
- No evidence of maternal cell contamination detected
- Detection limit: ~10% maternal DNA

SUMMARY
The familial TUBA1A c.197T>C p.(Val66Ala) variant associated with Lissencephaly was not detected in this fetal sample. Based on these results, the fetus is predicted to be unaffected by familial TUBA1A-related Lissencephaly.

LIMITATIONS
- This test specifically targets the known familial variant and does not exclude other potential genetic causes of Lissencephaly
- Maternal cell contamination below 10% cannot be excluded
- This analysis does not detect mosaicism below the sensitivity of Sanger sequencing (~20%)

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
